text: Hi, how's it going? I'm a big coffee lover, so I guess I'll start there. I can't really start my day without a cup of coffee, and this morning was no different. I had one before I came to take this test, and I'm already looking forward to another one once it's over. I work in IT, and my days are pretty busy. I live in an apartment, and I'm pretty much a homebody. In my free time, I like listening to music, playing computer games, and reading. So, yeah, that's me in a nutshell: coffee, music, and my computer. I'm happy to be here, and I hope I do well today!

Well, my favorite beach is a pebble beach near my home. It's only about 20 minutes from my place by car. It's not your typical sandy beach. Instead of sand, it's covered with smooth, round, black pebbles. That's what makes it special! When the waves come in and out, the stones make this soft, rolling sound. It's so relaxing, it's like a natural lullaby. Behind the beach, there's a row of old pine trees and a few small cafes. I go there once or twice a month, usually on weekends. To be honest, I go there more than anywhere else. Whenever I feel stressed out from work, that sound just washes it all away.

Most of the time, I go with a friend. We're kind of low-key people, so we don't do anything fancy. First, we grab two cups of coffee from a cafe nearby. Then we walk along the pebbles and find a bench facing the water. We just sit there and chat, or sometimes we don't say anything at all. I mean, we're totally fine with the silence. Sometimes I throw a few pebbles into the water, like a little kid. When other friends can join us, we bring snacks and make it a group day. One of them takes a million photos, and another just wants to eat. Anyway, for me, the beach is a place to slow down and recharge.

The last time I went was about a month ago, on a Sunday evening in the fall. I went with a friend, to the same beach again. It was a bit chilly, so we wore light jackets. The beach was almost empty. There were just a few couples and a man fishing at the far end. The sun was going down, and the whole sky turned orange and pink. It was gorgeous. We sat on the stones with our coffee and watched the sunset. The sound of the waves was so calming. I couldn't help but take a deep breath. Then my friend said, "We should do this more often." She's right. We stayed until it got dark, then we got some hot soup on the way home.

I live in an apartment in a small city by the sea. From the outside, it looks like a typical Korean apartment complex: tall, boxy buildings all in a row. But inside, it's pretty cozy. It has a few bedrooms, a living room, a kitchen, and two bathrooms. The living room is the heart of the house, because that's where my friends and I hang out. We have a big comfy sofa, and a TV that never seems to turn off! I also have my own little room with my computer and bookshelf. It's not huge, but it's just right for us. The best part is the sunlight. It gets great light all day, which is a huge plus!

Oh, I've had my share of problems. The first one is the classic: something breaks. Last year, the dishwasher stopped working, and we had dirty dishes piling up for days. Another time, the bathroom light kept flickering and drove me nuts. And then there's the "not cooperating" problem. I live with a roommate, and getting him to clean up his stuff is a daily battle! He leaves his clothes everywhere, and his game controllers on the floor. I step on them in the dark, and it hurts! But the biggest problem, by far, was a water leak in my bathroom ceiling. That one was a real headache.

The water leak is the one I remember best. It happened last summer. One morning, I walked into the bathroom and saw a big brown stain on the ceiling. Then, drip, drip, drip! Water was coming down. I thought, "Oh no, this is going to be a nightmare." I went upstairs and talked to my neighbor. It turned out that a pipe in their bathroom was cracked. Luckily, they were really nice about it. They called a plumber right away, and the building's insurance covered the repairs. It took about a week to fix. The plumber fixed the pipe and repainted our ceiling. I learned two things. First, stay calm. Second, be nice to your neighbors, because you never know when you'll need them!

My favorite delivery place is a little chicken shop near my apartment. The sign says "Crispy Chicken", which isn't very creative! But the chicken is amazing. They serve fried chicken, sweet and spicy chicken, and a half-and-half combo. I always go for the sweet and spicy. The shop itself is tiny. There are only two small tables, and the owner does everything himself. He's a really friendly guy. He always throws in a free soda or a bag of pickled radish. I love that place because the chicken is always hot and crispy, even after delivery. And honestly, the price is great, too. I order from there almost every Saturday night. It's become my little tradition.

The last time was this past Saturday. I was too tired to cook, so I opened the delivery app. I ordered the usual: sweet and spicy chicken, with fries and a big cola. Forty minutes later, the doorbell rang. I opened the box, and I couldn't believe it. It was the wrong order! They'd sent plain fried chicken with no sauce. I stared at that box like it had ruined my life. So I called the shop. The owner said, "I'm so sorry!" He sent out the right order in 20 minutes and told me to keep the first one for free. So I ended up with two chickens! I invited a neighbor over, and we ate until we couldn't move. It turned out to be a pretty good night.

A special time I remember was my friend's birthday. We wanted to throw him a small party at home, because he's a quiet man and hates big restaurants. So I decided to get raw fish from a local seafood place. That's his favorite. I called ahead and ordered a big platter for ten people. On the day, I drove to the restaurant to pick it up. When the owner handed me the box, it was huge! I carried it to the car like a baby. I drove really slowly the whole way home. When we opened it at the table, everybody said "Wow!" My friend smiled, which is rare! He said, "This is the best birthday ever." I almost cried. It was worth every minute.

Hi, I heard your store just opened near my apartment. Congratulations! I have a few questions about what you sell. First, what kinds of products do you have? Mostly vitamins, or do you have other things, too?. Okay. And do you sell protein powder or energy bars?. Great. What are your business hours? Are you open on weekends?. Also, do you offer delivery?. One last thing: do you have any special deals for new customers?. Awesome. That sounds perfect. I'll stop by this weekend. Thanks so much!

Hi, this is a customer. I bought a tub of protein powder at your store yesterday. I'm calling because there's a problem. When I got home and opened it, I noticed the safety seal was already broken. And the date on the bottom looks like it expired last month. I'm a little worried about eating it. I have the receipt right here. So, here's what I was thinking. First, could I bring it back and exchange it for a new one? Or, if you don't have any more in stock, I'd like a refund. Either one works for me. If it's easier, I can come by this afternoon. I really like your store, so I hope we can sort this out. Thanks for your help!

One meal I'll never forget was a company dinner a few years ago. My team and I were celebrating after finishing a huge project. We'd been working nights for months. Our boss said, "Dinner's on me." So we went to a crab restaurant by the sea here in my city. The owner brought out a giant snow crab. The thing is, none of us knew how to eat it properly! We were all making a total mess. Crab juice was flying everywhere! One guy got it right in his glasses. Everyone burst out laughing. Then the owner came over and showed us how to do it. We ended the night with spicy crab stew and rice. It was memorable because we were so tired and so happy at the same time.

Well, one change I've noticed is between Korea and Japan. When I was younger, the two countries didn't seem very friendly. There were a lot of tensions, and not many people traveled back and forth. But these days, it's a different story. Young people in Korea love Japanese food, anime, and travel. And a lot of Japanese people love K-pop and Korean dramas. A friend of mine has been to Japan twice just for shopping and cafes! There are also more direct flights and cheap tickets. I think culture is what brought people closer. It's hard to hate someone when you share the same favorite song. It's not perfect, but I'd say it's moving in a good direction.

I'd say the 2002 World Cup is a good example. Korea and Japan hosted it together, and that was a first in history. At the time, the two countries were still a little distant. So a lot of people were wondering if it would work. But it turned out to be a huge success. I remember watching the games with my friends and cheering so loudly that I lost my voice! Everywhere, people wore red shirts and the streets were packed. Japanese fans were cheering for Korea too, and it felt like something special was happening. It really opened the door for more cultural exchange, like music, movies, and travel. To this day, I still get goosebumps when I think about it.
